paper_title: Stronger limits on hypothetical Yukawa interactions in the 40--8000 nm range
notes: Paper constrains Yukawa-type fifth force (strength alpha relative to gravity vs range lambda in 30-8000 nm), a ScalarNucleon-type fifth force test. Exclusion limits are shown only in Fig. 4 (alpha vs lambda plane) with no numerical table or explicit text values, so no data points could be extracted reliably. The y-axis is alpha (Yukawa strength relative to gravity), not a standard dimensionless coupling, which complicates conversion. Mass conversion: lambda=hbar/mc, so range 30-8000 nm corresponds roughly to m ~ 6.6 eV down to 0.025 eV. | Vision: Figure 4 plots |alpha| (Yukawa strength relative to gravity) vs lambda (meters). Converted lambda to mass via m = hbar*c/lambda = 1.973e-7 eV*m / lambda. Red curve is this work's limit. The y-axis is the Yukawa alpha for nucleon-nucleon (ScalarNucleon-type fifth force) constraint. Note: original x-axis is length not mass; conversion applied. Mass range corresponds to lambda 30-8000 nm. Values approximate from log-log plot reading of the red curve. | Calibration: Spot-check calibration: verify/stage2 ratio=0.0x | Auto-corrected couplings: ×1.00e-08 (8 orders too large)
